title: Atomic Charge Chirality from Electric Multipoles
abstract: We establish an electric-multipole ($Q_{lm}$) criterion for chirality of local atomic charge distributions. For the 11 crystallographic chiral point groups, we identify representative lowest-rank multipole contents required to distinguish the opposite handednesses. For the axial groups $C_n$ and $D_n$ with $n=2,3,4,6$, chirality arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies with $m=n$, belonging to consecutive ranks $l=n$ and $n+1$. Their coexistence produces a latitude-dependent twist of the $n$-fold charge distribution. The polar component, although allowed in $C_n$, is distinct from this chiral mechanism and is not required for handedness. The cubic groups $T$ and $O$ exhibit distinct realizations, with octahedral chirality first appearing at rank nine. We further show that, within a spinless $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic basis, the scalar charge density contains multipoles only up to rank six and therefore cannot encode the handedness of $C_6$, $D_6$, or $O$. These results connect electric-multipole content and atomic orbital degrees of freedom to the microscopic encoding of crystallographic handedness.
summary: This theoretical work establishes a quantitative criterion using electric multipoles to determine the chirality of local atomic charge distributions in crystals. It shows that chirality is encoded by specific, relative orientations of multipoles belonging to consecutive angular momentum ranks. The findings provide a deep link between crystallographic symmetry and the microscopic electronic structure, while also highlighting limitations based on the available atomic orbital basis.
main_problem: The paper establishes an electric-multipole criterion to characterize the chirality of local atomic charge distributions within crystalline solids.
main_result: Chirality in axial groups ($C_n, D_n$) arises from the relative orientation of two azimuthal anisotropies at consecutive ranks ($l=n$ and $l=n+1$). Furthermore, the scalar charge density basis is insufficient to encode the handedness for high-symmetry groups like $C_6$ or $D_6$.
method: The analysis uses electric multipoles ($Q_{lm}$) and defines a pseudoscalar descriptor ($\chi_n$) that quantifies the relative orientation of anisotropic charge components, linking it to the absence of a common vertical mirror plane.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the charge density $ho(\mathbf{r})$ of atoms in crystalline structures, analyzing its symmetry properties based on crystallographic point groups ($C_n, D_n, T, O$). The analysis is restricted to a spinless $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic basis.
key_observables: The pseudoscalar handedness descriptor ($\chi_n$), the relative orientation of multipoles, and the rank of the required multipoles.
important_parameters: The azimuthal index $m=n$ and the consecutive ranks $l=n$ and $l=n+1$ are crucial for generating chirality in $C_n$ and $D_n$ groups.
main_assumptions: The analysis is limited to the scalar charge density and is constrained by the maximum rank (up to six) available in the $s$-$p$-$d$-$f$ atomic orbital basis.
figures_summary: Figure 1 visually demonstrates representative chiral charge distributions for tetragonal point groups ($D_4, C_4$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the electric-multipole criterion for chirality, then analyzes the minimal chiral combinations required for axial groups ($C_n, D_n$), discusses the distinct realizations in cubic groups ($T, O$), and concludes by detailing the limitations imposed by the atomic orbital basis.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state charge structure, the rigorous mathematical framework connecting symmetry operations (chirality) to the required angular momentum components (multipoles) is highly relevant to understanding symmetry breaking and electronic structure in correlated materials.
